attempted_claim: Let X_F subset P^4_Q be the Fermat quintic threefold x_0^5 + x_1^5 + x_2^5 + x_3^5 + x_4^5 = 0. Prove or disprove that every isolated line l on X_F is simple in the sense of Pauli and Espreafico-McKean-Pauli, i.e. its Segre plane quartic has three ordinary nodes and its Gauss double-point fibre is etale of degree 3. A complete answer either proves simplicity for all isolated lines via an explicit Gauss-discriminant computation, or exhibits one isolated line with explicit Plucker coordinates and a certified non-etale Gauss fibre such as a tacnode, cusp, or multiple component together with its higher Segre datum, and in either case records the exact simplicity or non-simplicity obstruction.
claim_type: universal simplicity versus explicit non-simple isolated line
decisive_failure: The isolation premise failed on the natural representative: l0 is a cone ruling with a 2-dimensional Fano tangent, and no exact rigid isolated line was located in 60 numeric starts. The authentic Pauli Segre-quartic construction was not recovered (the tangency resultant gives 7 lines with a multiplicity-7 point), and controlled literature retrieval failed, so neither target branch could be closed; the exact discriminant datum remains a routine byproduct.
domain: enriched enumerative geometry of special quintics
